name: Sanatkumāra's ladder to plenitude (ChU 7)
description: Nārada is led from name, through fourteen ever greater objects of veneration up to breath, then through a chain of conditions from truth to happiness, to plenitude and the self.

stages.name: nāma
stages.description: Venerate name as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: vāc
stages.description: Venerate speech as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: manas
stages.description: Venerate mind as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: saṅkalpa
stages.description: Venerate intention as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: citta
stages.description: Venerate thought as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Venerate meditation as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: vijñāna
stages.description: Venerate understanding as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: bala
stages.description: Venerate strength as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: anna
stages.description: Venerate food as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: āpas
stages.description: Venerate water as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: tejas
stages.description: Venerate heat as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: ākāśa
stages.description: Venerate space as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: smara
stages.description: Venerate memory as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: āśā
stages.description: Venerate hope as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: prāṇa
stages.description: Venerate breath as brahman; it is greater than the preceding rung and gives freedom of movement as far as it reaches.

stages.name: satya
stages.description: Truth must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: vijñāna
stages.description: Understanding must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: mati
stages.description: Reflection must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: śraddhā
stages.description: Faith must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: niṣṭhā
stages.description: Steadfastness must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: kṛti
stages.description: Action must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: sukha
stages.description: Happiness must be sought to be understood (each depends on the next).

stages.name: bhūman
stages.description: Where one sees, hears, understands nothing else: happiness, the immortal.

stages.name: ahaṃkārādeśa / ātmādeśa
stages.gloss: the teaching of 'I' and of the self
stages.description: Plenitude is all; I am all; the self is all; one who sees thus delights in the self and is self-ruled (svarāj); the knots are loosened and he is shown the far shore beyond darkness.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer: the fifteen rungs are meditative venerations (B2); the chain 16-22 is a regress of conditions, not a practice sequence, so no band is assigned.

name: The Kaṭha's inward withdrawal (KU 1.3.13)
description: A four-step withdrawal following the ladder of principles of KU 1.3.10-11, ending in the peaceful self.

stages.name: vāc → manas
stages.description: The wise one restrains speech in the mind.

stages.name: manas → jñāna ātman
stages.gloss: mind into the self that is knowledge
stages.description: Restrains that (mind) in the self that is knowledge (intellect).

stages.name: jñāna ātman → mahān ātmā
stages.description: Restrains knowledge in the great self.

stages.name: mahān → śānta ātman
stages.description: Restrains that in the peaceful self.

name: Prajāpati's four instructions to Indra (ChU 8.7-12)
description: Four successive teachings over 32 + 32 + 32 + 5 = 101 years, each tested by Indra until the last.

stages.name: the person seen in the eye / the reflected body
stages.description: Taught first; Virocana stops here and teaches the asuras that the body is the self; Indra sees the flaw.

stages.name: the one who moves about in dreams
stages.description: Not harmed by the body's defects, but seems to suffer.

stages.name: the one fully asleep, serene, seeing no dream
stages.description: Then one does not know oneself or beings, 'gone to annihilation as it were'.

stages.name: the serene one who reaches the highest light
stages.gloss: the bodiless self in its own form
stages.description: The body is the mortal base of the immortal bodiless self; rising from it, reaching the highest light, it appears in its own form.

notes: Stages 2-3 are provisional teachings, not practices; no band assigned. Advaita reads the sequence as superimposition and retraction (U13).

name: Bhṛgu's five realizations (TU 3)
description: Seeking brahman by tapas, as defined by Varuṇa (that from which beings arise, live and return), Bhṛgu understands brahman successively as food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss (cf. the five selves of TU 2).

stages.name: annaṃ brahma
stages.description: Understood by tapas; returns to Varuṇa.

stages.name: ānando brahma
stages.description: The knowledge of Bhṛgu and Varuṇa, established in the highest heaven.

stages.name: the knower's song
stages.gloss: moving through the worlds singing 'I am food'
stages.description: Having passed into the five selves, the knower moves through the worlds eating what he wishes and taking what form he wishes, singing.

notes: Stages 1-4 are successive understandings within one inquiry; bands assigned only to the last two.

name: Learning, childlikeness, silence (BAU 3.5.1)
description: The stages of the knower who has renounced, as stated to Kahola.

stages.name: vyutthāna
stages.description: Knowing the self, brahmins rise above the desires for sons, wealth and worlds and live as mendicants.

stages.name: pāṇḍitya
stages.description: Having done with learning ...

stages.name: bālya
stages.description: ... he should live as a child.

stages.name: mauna
stages.description: Having done with childhood and learning, he becomes a silent sage.

stages.name: brāhmaṇa
stages.description: Having done with silence and non-silence, he becomes a brahmin.

notes: The meaning of bālya (childlike state; Śaṅkara relates it to the strength of knowledge) is not settled; no band.
